simple.meaning: מְגֵרָה (mᵉgêrâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a saw.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 2 Samuel 12:31. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מְגֵרָה (H4050) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מְגֵרָה (mᵉgêrâh) / H4050 is traced through 2 Samuel 12:31, 1 Kings 7:9, 1 Chronicles 20:3 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He brought out the people who were in it, and put them under saws, under iron picks, under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brick kiln; and he did so to all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

definitions.full: H4050. megerah מְגֵרָה noun feminine saw (Late Hebrew id. , perhaps from its harsh dragging sound) — מְגֵרָה 2Sam 12:31 a + 2 t.; plural מְגֵרוֺת 1Chr 20:3 (< מַגְזְרוֺת 2Sam 12:31 b) — saw , used in cutting stone בַּמְּגֵרָה מְגֹרָרוֺת 1Kin 7:9 ; used in torture (or as tools for enforced labour) of captives 2Sam 12:31 a 1Chr 20:3 a.
